slots.title: Fed holds target at 4% after 3.8%
slots.body:
The Fed’s Sept. 16 decision landed at a 4% target — matching the 4% estimate and above the prior 3.8% setting.

Coverage after the call described Warsh as stressing that rates may not be holding growth back yet and pointing to the energy shock as part of the inflation picture.

U.S. indexes closed lower into that headline stack:

- $SPY proxy ^GSPC −0.4% to 7,553.33  
- Dow ^DJI −1.2% (−631.21 pts) to 51,461.90  
- Nasdaq ^IXIC −0.0% to 25,978.42

The volatility gauge ^VIX finished at 17.71, up 3.0% on the session.

The 10-year Treasury yield sat at 5.0% in the latest curve snapshot (Sept. 14 dated).

What stood out most to you in the post-meeting messaging — rates, energy, or something else?

slots.title: August retail sales +1.4% vs +0.4% est.
slots.body:
August U.S. retail sales (month-over-month change in spending at stores and online) printed at +1.4%.

That was roughly triple the +0.4% estimate and flipped from July’s −0.4% reading.

The year-over-year pace came in at +6% vs a +4.7% estimate (prior +5.0%).

Excluding autos, spending was also +1.4% MoM vs a +0.5% estimate.

Excluding gas and autos, the MoM gain was +1.2% vs a +0.2% estimate.

Those prints hit the wire on Sept. 16, the same session the Fed held rates at 4% and major indexes closed mixed to lower.

Which slice of the report do you watch first — headline, ex-autos, or the year-over-year line?

slots.title: GDPNow Q3 tracking rises to 5.1%
slots.body:
The Atlanta Fed GDPNow reading for Q3 U.S. GDP growth — a running estimate built from incoming data — updated to 5.1% on Sept. 16.

That beat the 4.4% estimate slot and moved up from the prior 4.4% print on the calendar.

It landed the same day August retail sales showed a +1.4% MoM gain vs a +0.4% estimate and +6% YoY vs +4.7% expected.

Session context from the prior close:

- S&P 500 ^GSPC −0.4% to 7,553.33  
- Dow ^DJI −1.2% to 51,461.90

Do you treat GDPNow as a check on hard data releases, or mostly as background noise?

slots.title: U.S. session recap — Sept. 16, 2026
slots.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 51,461.90, down 631.21 points (-1.2%), the largest index decline among the major U.S. benchmarks on the session.

The S&P 500 finished at 7,553.33 (-32.40 points, -0.4%).
The Nasdaq Composite was essentially flat at 25,978.42 (-3.15, 0.0%).
The Russell 2000 closed at 2,858.81 (-11.47, -0.4%).

The Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision showed an actual target of 4%, matching the 4% estimate and up from 3.8% previously, followed by FOMC economic projections and a high-impact press conference the same evening.

August retail sales data printed stronger than expected: retail sales year-over-year at 6% (estimate 4.7%), month-over-month at 1.4% (estimate 0.4%), ex-gas/autos MoM at 1.2% (estimate 0.2%), and ex-autos MoM at 1.4% (estimate 0.5%).

The Atlanta Fed GDPNow reading for Q3 was 5.1%, above the 4.4% estimate and prior 4.4% figure.

Sector performance on Nasdaq was led higher by Industrials at +2.4% average change.
Healthcare was +0.2%.
Technology averaged -0.6%.
Financial Services averaged -1.8%.
Communication Services averaged -1.1%.
Energy averaged -2.8%, the weakest sector in the set.

Among large caps, $BAC closed at 57.90 (-2.7%), $JPM at 348.92 (-1.0%), and $MA at 567.75 (-1.0%).
$CVX was 211.52 (-2.9%).
$NFLX was 76.41 (-1.9%).
$GOOGL was 342.87 (-0.6%).
$AAPL was 332.41 (+0.3%).
$NVDA was 213.90 (+0.8%), $TSM 417.72 (+1.0%), and $ASML 1,602.22 (+0.7%).

Lennar ($LEN) reported earnings for the date: EPS actual 1.23 versus estimate 1.28, revenue actual $8.00B versus estimate about $8.32B; the stock closed at 78.36 (-2.1%).

The CBOE Volatility Index ($VIX) rose to 17.71 (+0.51, +3.0%).
Gold futures ($GCUSD) were 4,323.10 (-64.40, -1.5%).
$USO finished 156.17 (-3.5%).
The Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund ($UUP) was 28.40 (+0.6%).
Bitcoin ($BTCUSD) was 76,402.83 (+0.3%).

Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-09-14) showed the 10-year at 5.0% and the 2s10s spread at 0.32 percentage points.

Overseas references in the data included the FTSE 100 at 10,688.47 (+0.3%), the Hang Seng at 24,443.00 (-1.1%), and the Nikkei 225 at 63,966.87 (+0.1%).

slots.title: August housing starts MoM: +9.0% est.
slots.body:
Thursday 12:30 p.m.
ET: Housing Starts for August.

MoM change — consensus +9.0%.

Prior month: -12.4%.

Level — consensus 1.31M annualized units.

Prior level: 1.24M (1.239M in the calendar).

The MoM figure is the pace of change in new-home construction; the level is how many starts that pace implies over a full year.

Same release window as building permits and jobless claims.
